Topic: Carried question: do different tests agree?
Story (story.md): Same data, more than one rule. Do they agree? Disagree? When does it matter?
Technical (chapter.md): Opening carry-over from Ch 3: same data, multiple tests, when do they converge or diverge?

Topic: Sally Clark and the cost of picking the wrong procedure
Story (story.md): 1999 conviction: prosecution squared 1/8500 to get '1 in 73 million' SIDS. RSS criticized 2001, overturned 2003. Same data, different assumption, different verdict.
Technical (chapter.md): Motivating framing for why procedure choice matters.

Topic: The family of tests we'll use
Story (story.md): Narrator names them informally: honest count, bell-curve approximation, proxy-crowd, t-test, belief curve.
Technical (chapter.md): Framing list: exact binomial, normal-approx z, chi-square GoF, Fisher exact (force-fitted one-sample), one-sample t, plus Bayesian conjugate counterpart.

Topic: Honest count as the baseline
Story (story.md): Introduced as 'the rule that came naturally' — count fair-coin outcomes at least as extreme as k.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Try: exact binomial under H0: p=0.5 is the gold standard.

Topic: Bell-curve approximation: why it exists
Story (story.md): Motivated by pre-computer cost: normal tails are closed-form, table-lookup cheap. Trade accuracy at the tails for speed.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Try: normal-approx z treats the binomial as asymptotically normal.

Topic: 60/100 boundary split between procedures
Story (story.md): Worked example: honest count 0.057, bell-curve 0.046. Same data, opposite sides of alpha=0.05, different verdicts.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Observe (60/100): exact 0.057, z 0.046, chi-square 0.046, Fisher 0.201, t 0.045.

Topic: Three observations at a glance
Story (story.md): Three-panel log-scale chart at 6/10, 60/100, 600/1000. Agreement at extremes, split at borderline. Image story/same_data_three_views.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Observe: p-value grid across 6/10, 60/100, 600/1000, 6000/10000. Image pvalue_grid.png.

Topic: 600/1000 and larger: everyone rejects
Story (story.md): Both honest count and bell-curve give ~3e-10. Both reject easily. Proxy-crowd still rejects but 40,000x weaker.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Observe: at 600/1000, exact/z/chi-square/t ~1e-10; Fisher 8.45e-6. At 6000/10000, Fisher ~40 orders of magnitude weaker than others.

Topic: Gap between honest count and bell-curve shrinks like 1/sqrt(N)
Story (story.md): Per-N curves across every possible observation: gap 0.23 at n=10, 0.11 at n=50, 0.025 at n=1000. Image story/bell_vs_honest_gap.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Try/Observe: absolute gap across (k,n) for n in {10,25,50,100,250,500,1000}. Image normal_vs_exact.png.

Topic: Textbook 'np>=5, n(1-p)>=5' rule is necessary but not sufficient
Story (story.md): At p=0.5 the rule says N>=10 is fine; chart shows gap still 0.08 at N=100 and 0.025 at N=1000. Need N in the thousands for 1% agreement.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Rule of thumb: same conclusion, prefer exact when feasible — modern computers don't care.

Topic: Proxy-crowd procedure: Fisher force-fitted to one sample
Story (story.md): Pair observation (k, n-k) with an idealized fair reference and run 2x2 Fisher. Adds imaginary noise, answers a slightly different question.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A framing: Fisher exact on observed vs (n/2, n/2) reference is the wrong tool on purpose.

Topic: Proxy-crowd converges to exact as reference grows
Story (story.md): Narrator notes: as the proxy crowd grows, Fisher converges toward the honest count because imaginary noise vanishes.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Observe: at 60/100, Fisher with ref size n=100 is 0.201; 10n is 0.059; 100n is 0.056, converging to exact 0.057.

Topic: Chi-square GoF and z-test are the same test for binary data
Story (story.md): Flagged late: chi-square for two-bin observations equals z-squared; identical p-values.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Note: chi-square statistic equals z^2 and chi-square(1) reference is squared standard normal. They generalize differently but collapse here.

Topic: One-sample t-test on 0/1 data
Story (story.md): Introduced only through its failure mode at boundaries.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A framing: one-sample t with mu_null=0.5 on the 0/1 sequence. On 0/1 data SE is p_hat(1-p_hat)n/(n-1); Wald-style proportion test with SE from data not null.

Topic: Boundary observations: where procedures fall over
Story (story.md): Five extreme cases (1/1, 0/10, 10/10, 0/100, 100/100). Image story/boundary_breakdown.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop C Try: 0/10, 10/10, 1/1, 0/100, 100/100 through all five tests. Image edge_cases.png.

Topic: At 1/1 the t-test returns NaN
Story (story.md): t-test cannot compute sample variance with one point; returns undefined.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop C Observe: t-test returns NaN at 1/1; the only test that fails to produce a number. Other four approach p=1 correctly.

Topic: At 0/N or N/N the t-test returns zero with infinite t-statistic
Story (story.md): All-heads variance is zero → divide-by-zero gives infinite t, p=0. Procedure claims infinite surprise — wrong.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop C Observe: at 0/10 and 10/10, t returns p=0 with infinite t; exact says ~0.002 (2/1024).

Topic: Edge-case hunch: prefer exact when in doubt
Story (story.md): Story closing the boundary section: 'I should know the assumptions of whatever procedure I am using, and I should know where it lies. The honest count does not lie, because it does not approximate.'
Technical (chapter.md): Loop C Hunch: when in doubt, prefer the exact test. Use approximations for speed when N is large enough.

Topic: Belief curve: the Bayesian lens on the same data
Story (story.md): Three panels at 6/10, 60/100, 600/1000: widening-then-narrowing belief curves with 95% bands. Image story/belief_alongside.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Try/Observe: Beta(1,1) prior then posterior at 6/10, 60/100, 600/1000, 6000/10000. Image bayes_alongside.png.

Topic: Belief curve values at 6/10, 60/100, 600/1000
Story (story.md): Bands: 0.32-0.81 (6/10), 0.50-0.69 (60/100 just barely excluding fair), 0.57-0.63 (600/1000 far from fair).
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Observe: Beta(7,5) centre 0.583 CI [0.32,0.81]; Beta(61,41) centre 0.598 CI [0.50,0.69]; Beta(601,401) centre 0.60 CI [0.57,0.63].

Topic: Borderline data is where disputes live
Story (story.md): The 60/100 row: reasonable analysts could disagree. Pharma p=0.04 vs 0.06, limbic encephalitis 0.01 vs 0.08, financial regulation population choice.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Compare: frequentist family itself splits at alpha=0.05 at 60/100; Bayesian CI's lower bound right at 0.50.

Topic: Pre-commit to a procedure before seeing data
Story (story.md): Rule: commit to a procedure in advance
Technical (chapter.md): as you would a sample size. Flexibility invites fishing.
Code: Implicit methodology point underpinning Loop A.

Topic: Overcounting the family: really three or four procedures
Story (story.md): Narrator admits 'five tests' was overcounting; real list is three or four genuinely different.
Technical (chapter.md): Same collapse noted in Loop A Note (chi-square vs z).

Topic: From tests to intervals: the dual
Story (story.md): Tests answer one specific null; often we want a range. Every test has a confidence-interval dual.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Forward pointer: each test has a confidence-interval dual; Ch 5 turns the family inside-out into intervals.

Story (story.md): Closing line opening Ch 5.
